newsitem.title: FRANCE: KAL ups Paris-Seoul air cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: KAL ups Paris-Seoul air cargo capacity.

text.p: Korean Airlines (KAL) said its plan to introduce an extra passenger frequency between Paris-Seoul will mean more freight capacity becoming available on the route.
The extra flight, effective July 5, will increase KAL's Paris-Seoul passenger flights to five a week.

"Unlike cargo capacity on the existing passenger flights, KAL will share bellyhold space on the extra frequency 50-50 with Air France, with each airline having roughly seven tonnes," the official told Reuters.
He added: "Departing from Paris-CDG late on Saturday evening, the supplementary cargo capacity will be particularly handy for freight trucked in from provincial centres.
"This does not arrive in time to catch our joint Boeing 747 full-freighter service with Air France which leaves a couple of hours earlier," he said."
KAL and Air France are currently considering raising their Paris-Seoul 747F frequencies to three from two a week, the official added.
